newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: P.Lehman to improve wine-making facilities.
newsitem.headline: P.Lehman to improve wine-making facilities.

text.p: Peter Lehmann Wines Ltd said on Tuesday it would spend nearly A$1.46 million in 1997/98, funded from the final conversion of options in November, on improving facilities to maintain an edge as a quality wine producer.

Peter Lehmann, which earlier announced a 43 percent rise in net profit for 1996/97 to A$2.5 million, said its total intake for the 1997 vintage of 12,500 tonnes of grapes was 13 percent down on the previous year.
However, the shortfall on budgeted purchased fruit was confined to the less preferred varieties, and all premium varieties achieved or exceeded budgeted tonnages.
"This will enable (Peter Lehmann) to build up stock to meet future sales demand," the company said in a statement.
Peter Lehman said rises in grape prices in 1997 had put pressure on margins but it had selectively increased bottle wine pricing without adversely affecting sales volumes.
With demand for red grapes in particular remaining high, further price increases for the 1998 vintage could not be ruled out but it believed there may be some easing in white grape prices, it said.
The company said although dry weather conditions in June and July had eased with early August rains, but it was essential for the 1998 harvest that followup rains came in the ensuing months.
Peter Lehman shares were four cents firmer at A$1.62 at 1.55 p.m. (0355 GMT).
